key_insight: V-PaSS improves extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar-cell performance by encoding absorber solid-solution physics and device-stack semantics instead of treating materials and layers as simple categories.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable screening of new perovskite compositions and unfamiliar device architectures before fabrication, reducing costly trial-and-error in solar-cell design.
method: Interpolates mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers from 23 relaxed pure ABX3 endpoint crystal graphs using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing.
Represents the device stack with layer order, cell polarity, interfacial band offsets, and chemical text embeddings from a scientific language model.
Uses an institution-grouped evaluation protocol to test true out-of-lab extrapolation on unseen laboratories, alloys, and transport-layer combinations.
evidence_signal: Under unseen-laboratory splits, the untuned default V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE, beating the best gradient-boosted baseline (3.017%) and the best tuned benchmark (2.912%), with larger gains on unseen alloys and transport layers.
watch_item: Performance depends on having physically meaningful endpoint crystal graphs and reliable interfacial/band-offset descriptors, which may limit transfer when such inputs are unavailable or uncertain.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
